reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend with holidays and introduces a shared isNonWorkingDay that every path uses, but there is no shared 'adjust one occurrence' function, so getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template each recompose the daily-skip vs move decision.

duplication.why: The per-occurrence rule (daily+skipWeekend => drop non-working days, else move with getDateWithSkippedWeekend) is written out in getUpcomingDates and again in getDatesInRange, and a third time as isDaily/movedForWeekend in schedule-template.ts, besides the getNextDate branch.

placement.why: Holiday/weekend predicates and moving live in shared/schedules.ts as they should, but the daily-vs-other dispatch is decided in server handlers and the budget template instead of in the shared module.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps (daily skip, range handler, holidays, yearly holidays) plus tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: isNonWorkingDay keeps the holiday definition in one place, but changing how daily schedules treat non-working days still means editing four call paths that each encode the dispatch differently (including the noSkipWeekend=!isDaily trick).

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and server/budget/schedule-template.ts, compute config.skipWeekend && frequency==='daily' themselves rather than going through getNextDate/a shared occurrence-adjust helper.

disguised_duplication.where: The occurrence-adjust block in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (schedules/app.ts) is the same logic reshaped (nested ifs vs early continue); schedule-template.ts re-expresses it as movedForWeekend/nextOccurrence closures.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained a holidays parameter and schedule data gained isDaily/holidays; getNextDate gained a daily special-case branch; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template createScheduleList each re-decide the daily skip themselves.
